title: Functions Practice: Tip Calculator
story: You're out to dinner with friends. The bill arrives — $80. How much should everyone tip? Instead of pulling out your phone's calculator (which is basically cheating when you're a programmer), you build your own tip calculator out of functions!
why: Building a real-world tool with multiple functions proves you understand how to compose functions together to solve practical problems.
analogy: A tip calculator is like assembling a meal — each function is a separate step (chop vegetables, cook protein, plate the dish), and main is the chef who puts all the steps together.
try_it: Add a `split_bill(total: Int, people: Int) -> Int` function that divides the total by the number of people. Print how much each person owes!
tips: Functions can call other functions — `print_bill` calls both `calc_tip` and `calc_total`
Keep calculation functions pure: `calc_tip` just returns a number, it doesn't print anything
Use a separate function for formatting/printing — this lets you reuse the calculation functions in other programs
common_mistakes: Putting the calculation AND printing in one function — separate them so you can calculate tips even when you don't want to print
Using Int division incorrectly — `amount * percent / 100` works because multiplication happens before division
